summary: Phase 149O.20L.2 -- Full-HBDC Readiness Contract / Schema Independent Verification. Verification-only: no production, contract, HBDC-001, or HMIC-001 change was made by this phase; no Class-B provisioning; no certification/activation. Independently verified HMRC-001 v1.1's Full-HBDC readiness contract/schema evolution (Phase 149O.20L.1), trusting none of that phase's report, tests, six-vs-seven classification, eight-term readiness design, HMRC-REQ-086-100 wording, closed-enum mapping, attack-matrix update, or schema/backward-compatibility conclusions -- every claim below was independently re-derived from fixed git history, current HMRC-001 v1.1 text, current production source, and primary contract text. Confirmed via git log that exactly two commits have ever touched HMRC-001 (945af762, the v1.0 freeze; 582226b1, the v1.1 amendment), with f14e524e as the true immediate pre-amendment commit. Read v1.0's HMRC-REQ-054 directly at 945af762: exactly six bullets, none mentioning repository_instance_id. Read hatp_mandatory_cutover.py directly: the seven-check readiness-assembly function (_assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root) was introduced at Phase 149O.18F (commit 861fb04f), which pre-dates the HMRC-001 v1.1 amendment by many phases -- independently confirming the six-vs-seven discrepancy existed in live production well before 149O.20L.1's repair. Independently classified the seventh live term (repository_deployment_identity_valid) as contract drift grounded in HATP-REQ-052 (read directly: binds repository_id), not an ungoverned addition -- v1.1's in-place repair of HMRC-REQ-054 to seven bullets is correct, matching the git-diff evidence that no attack-matrix row and no other requirement text was removed in the amendment. Confirmed class_b_protected_storage_available is computed solely as protected_root.is_dir() and not protected_root.is_symlink() -- a strict subset of the ~24 HBDC-REQ checks verify_class_b_deployment_conformance() aggregates, and confirmed zero production consumer of that function anywhere outside its own defining module -- the new eighth term is genuinely distinct, not a restatement. Independently re-read ClassBConformanceStatus directly from hatp_class_b_topology_verifier.py: exactly six members (COMPLIANT, NON_COMPLIANT, INDETERMINATE, ACCESS_ERROR, MALFORMED_STATE, UNSUPPORTED_DEPLOYMENT_MODEL), all six covered by HMRC-REQ-088's mapping table inside its code fence, only COMPLIANT mapped true. Independently read certification_status_satisfies_readiness directly: 'return status is CertificationStatus.VALID' -- the exact-identity, non-truthiness precedent HMRC-REQ-088 explicitly mirrors. Confirmed HMRC-REQ-089 requires identity-to-COMPLIANT (not negative membership against known failures), so unknown/future/erroring status values fail closed by construction, not by an incomplete enumeration that could fall through on a future enum extension. Verified directly against contract text: evidence/Boolean separation (HMRC-REQ-090, requires 'detail' to name the exact ClassBConformanceStatus value); freshness/no-cache (HMRC-REQ-092); lock-held re-evaluation via the existing _write_cutover_transition/readiness_check callback with explicitly no separate lock (HMRC-REQ-093, cross-checked against the real function's source, which re-invokes the same assessment function while the transition lock is held); TOCTOU/staleness closure (HMRC-REQ-094); no caller-override surface (HMRC-REQ-095, independently confirmed zero class_b_ok/class_b_status-shaped parameter exists anywhere in current hatp_mandatory_cutover.py source); AND-conjunction with no alternate ready-via-Class-B-alone path (HMRC-REQ-096, cross-checked against the real ready=(len(unmet_reasons)==0) aggregation); HMIC/Class-B independence (HMRC-REQ-097); and the HBDC-001 non-amendment relationship (HMRC-REQ-098, HBDC-REQ-049/055/CBD-8 read directly from HBDC-001, confirmed unchanged and consistent with the new prerequisite). Attack matrix independently re-verified: exactly 52 rows present, sequential 1-52 with no gaps or duplicates (mechanically extracted, not counted from prose), none of the original 45 rows' text altered (row-by-row diff against the pre-149O.20L.1 baseline), and all 7 required new failure classes present in rows 46-52 (NON_COMPLIANT, INDETERMINATE, malformed/unknown/exception, stale advisory COMPLIANT reuse, caller-supplied override attempt, omitted evaluation, COMPLIANT-plus-another-term-false). Requirement numbering HMRC-REQ-001 through HMRC-REQ-100 confirmed gapless by mechanical extraction. Version-bump (v1.0 to v1.1, minor, in-place) confirmed correct by direct analogy to HMIC-001's own v1.0-to-v1.1 precedent (149O.19.5E.1: also a widening, no-removal amendment), and independently confirmed no existing HMRC-REQ definition line was removed in the amendment diff (only HMRC-REQ-054 itself was repaired in place, as expected). Regression-checked and reconfirmed, not re-litigated: B-149O.20L.1-1 remains INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT HMIC DESCRIPTIVE CONTRACT-IDENTITY CONSISTENCY BOUNDARY (HMIC-001's own Depends-on header line independently re-read: 'HMRC-001 v1.1'; derive_contract_versions independently re-read: parses the live '**Version:**' header via regex, not a hardcoded literal). CBV-S1 remains INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED CLOSED AT HMIC CONTRACT + PRODUCTION SOURCE-IDENTITY BOUNDARY (28 authority-bearing files via the live module-level assert, 5 contract-identity members via the live _CONTRACT_IDENTITY_FILES tuple, both independently re-counted from current source, unchanged; all three Class-B verifier modules still bound in HMIC-REQ-050's live text). Independent fixed-commit baseline: an isolated, disposable git worktree at the true pre-149O.20L.1 commit (f14e524e) reproduced 124 failed / 6908 passed / 5 skipped / 10 errors on pytest -m fast_green -n auto, and 89 failed / 2657 passed / 7 skipped on the broad -k 'hmrc or readiness or class_b or hbdc or 149o_20l' sweep. The current tree (pre-this-phase's-own-commits) produced 24 new fast_green node-ID deltas and 11 new broad-sweep deltas beyond that baseline (zero resolved in either comparison, taken via exact sorted comm -13/-23 set difference, never count-only). Every one of the 24 fast_green deltas was individually attributed: 23 are historical-pin/fixed-commit-self-check assertions of the literal form 'HMRC-001 is byte-unchanged/v1.0/45-rows/001-through-085-gapless since a fixed commit' -- legitimate, expected, disclosed consequences of HMRC-001's first-ever amendment, directly analogous to 149O.20L.1's own prior citation of the same failure family -- and the remaining one (tests/test_shell_gate.py::TestAuditPersistence::test_audit_verify_cli) was independently confirmed an environmental concurrency flake by reproducing the entire TestAuditPersistence class standalone outside -n auto (7/7 pass, including the companion test that had itself flipped pass/fail between the two -n auto runs). Clean-deselected fast_green citation (157-node argv-list --deselect via Python subprocess argv, never shell string interpolation): 0 failed, 7036 passed, 5 skipped, 1 pre-existing fido2 collection error (tests/test_phase_149o_7_..., missing 'fido2' hardware module, unrelated and unchanged from every prior phase's citation -- a collection-time import error is not deselectable by node ID). Constructed a fresh, independent bypass proof (not copied from 149O.20L.1's own fixture): monkeypatched verify_class_b_deployment_conformance with a call-counting wrapper and directly invoked _assess_hatp_mandatory_activation_readiness_at_root -- confirmed zero invocations, proving live production's readiness assessment genuinely never evaluates Class-B conformance at all, independently confirming the eighth-term production-integration gap (149O.20L.3) remains genuinely necessary, not merely asserted. Wrote a new, independent 63-test module (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_2_full_hbdc_readiness_contract_schema_independent_verification.py) that imports none of 149O.20L.1's tests; all 63 pass, both standalone and under -n auto. Disclosed two narrow, non-blocking contract-text staleness defects found during the internal-consistency sweep, neither security-relevant, neither fixed in this verification-only phase: HMRC-REQ-082 (Section 31, Implementation Readiness) still cites 'the 45-scenario attack matrix is frozen (Section 29)' though Section 29 was widened to 52 scenarios at v1.1 and the header/§30/§37 were all correctly updated; Section 35 ('Next Phase') still names the long-completed Phase 149O.16 and 'all 45 attacks' as unedited v1.0-freeze boilerplate never touched by the v1.1 amendment. Recommends a narrow, same-version Phase 149O.20L.2A repair updating both citations in place, mirroring the B-149O.20L.1-1/149O.20L.1A precedent -- explicitly not patched opportunistically in this verification-only phase per governing instructions. HMRC-001 v1.1: FULL-HBDC READINESS CONTRACT / SCHEMA INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED. B-149O.20L.1-1 remains unchanged, independently reconfirmed closed. CBV-S1 remains unchanged, independently reconfirmed closed. CBV-S10 remains OPEN -- READINESS CONTRACT INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED -- PRODUCTION INTEGRATION + INDEPENDENT PRODUCTION VERIFICATION PENDING (does not close here). Production readiness: still exactly seven terms, no eighth check, no Class-B verifier call -- independently reconfirmed against live source and confirmed correctly disclosed as unwired by the contract's own Section 37.8. Class-B: NOT PROVISIONED. HATP production: NOT READY. Runtime: Observed / observe / unavailable.
